blocks.title: Policy-overlap factor
blocks.body:
For a real parameter \(\zeta\), define the policy-overlap constant \(L\) by
\[
L(\zeta)=\exp(\zeta).
\]

blocks.title: Full finite trajectory
blocks.body:
For natural numbers \(T,n_X,n_H\), a full trajectory of length \(T\) is a pair
\[
\bigl((S_t)_{t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}},((A_t,Y_t))_{t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}}\bigr)
\in
\bigl(\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times \{0,\ldots,n_H-1\}\bigr)^{\{0,\ldots,T\}}
\times
\bigl(\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\times \mathbb R\bigr)^{\{0,\ldots,T-1\}} .
\]
Here \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\) is the observed--latent joint state at state time \(t\), with observed coordinate \(X_t\in\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\) and latent coordinate \(H_t\in\{0,\ldots,n_H-1\}\). At transition time \(t\), \(A_t\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\) is the Boolean action and \(Y_t\in\mathbb R\) is the reward; when actions are written numerically, \(\mathrm{false}\) is identified with \(0\) and \(\mathrm{true}\) with \(1\).

blocks.title: Markov kernel
blocks.body:
For each \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\),
\[
\mathcal L(Y_t,X_{t+1},H_{t+1}\mid X_{0:t},H_{0:t},A_{0:t},Y_{0:t-1})
=
K(\cdot\mid X_t,H_t,A_t).
\]

blocks.title: Memoryless binary policy carrier
blocks.body:
For \(n_X\in\mathbb N\), a memoryless policy on an observed-state alphabet of size \(n_X\) is a function
\[
p:\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\to\mathbb R .
\]
When the action alphabet is written as \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), we identify \(\mathrm{false}\) with \(0\) and \(\mathrm{true}\) with \(1\). This is a carrier only: no nonnegativity and no normalization is imposed here. The probability-vector restrictions on the behavior and target carriers are imposed later, on \(b\) in \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability} and on \(e\) in \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap}.

blocks.title: Observed-state sequential ignorability
blocks.body:
Identify the numeric action alphabet \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) with the Boolean action set by \(0\leftrightarrow \mathrm{false}\) and \(1\leftrightarrow \mathrm{true}\). The behavior carrier \(b\) is a probability vector at each observed state,
\[
b(a\mid x)\ge 0
\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X,\ a\in\mathcal A,
\qquad
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A} b(a\mid x)=1
\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X.
\]
For every \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\), the joint law of the state-and-epoch history strictly before \(t\), the current joint state \((X_t,H_t)\), and the current action \(A_t\) factors as the law of that history and current joint state followed by the behavior kernel evaluated at the current observed state:
\[
\mathbb P\!\left\{
\bigl((X_s,H_s)_{s<t},(A_s,Y_s)_{s<t},(X_t,H_t),A_t\bigr)\in dh\,da
\right\}
=
\mathbb P\!\left\{
\bigl((X_s,H_s)_{s<t},(A_s,Y_s)_{s<t},(X_t,H_t)\bigr)\in dh
\right\}
\, b(da\mid X_t(h)).
\]
Equivalently, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\),
\[
\Pr\!\left(A_t=a\mid X_{0:t},H_{0:t},A_{0:t-1},Y_{0:t-1}\right)
=
b(a\mid X_t).
\]

blocks.title: Policy transition operator
blocks.body:
For a raw experiment \(M\) with one-step kernel \(K\), a memoryless policy \(p\), and joint states \(s=(x,h)\) and \(s'\), define the policy-induced transition operator \(P_p\) by
\[
P_p(s,s')
:=
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}
p(a\mid x)\,
K\bigl(\{(r,\widetilde s): \widetilde s=s'\}\mid s,a\bigr).
\]

blocks.title: Joint-state alphabet
blocks.body:
For natural numbers \(n_X\) and \(n_H\), the finite observed--latent joint-state alphabet is
\[
\mathcal S(n_X,n_H)
:=
\{i\in\mathbb N: 0\le i<n_X\}
\times
\{j\in\mathbb N: 0\le j<n_H\}.
\]

blocks.title: Behavior and target stationary joint-state laws
blocks.body:
For a memoryless policy \(p\in\{b,e\}\), let \(P_p\) be the policy-induced Markov kernel on the joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\). Define \(d_p\in\Delta(\mathcal S)\) to be the stationary joint-state law satisfying
\[
d_pP_p=d_p .
\]
We write \(d_b\) for the behavior-policy stationary joint-state law and \(d_e\) for the target-policy stationary joint-state law.

blocks.title: Stationary start
blocks.body:
The initial joint state \(S_0\) has the behavior stationary law \(d_b\):
\[
S_0\sim d_b.
\]

blocks.title: Bounded rewards
blocks.body:
For each \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\),
\[
\Pr(|Y_t|\le 1)=1.
\]

blocks.title: Policy overlap
blocks.body:
The target carrier \(e\) is a probability vector at each observed state,
\[
e(a\mid x)\ge 0
\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X,\ a\in\mathcal A,
\qquad
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A} e(a\mid x)=1
\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X,
\]
and for every \((a,x)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal X\) the policy-overlap constant \(L\) satisfies
\[
e(a\mid x)\le L b(a\mid x).
\]

blocks.title: Derived contraction factor
blocks.body:
For any real \(t_0\), define the contraction parameter \(\alpha\) by
\[
\alpha := \exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{t_0}\right).
\]

blocks.title: Uniform contraction
blocks.body:
For every \((p,
u,
u')\in\{b,e\}	imes\Delta(\mathcal S)^2\), the contraction parameter \(\alpha\) and the policy-induced transition operator \(P_p\) satisfy
\[
\|
u P_p-
u'P_p\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le
\alpha\|
u-
u'\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]

blocks.title: Latent stationary overlap
blocks.body:
For the overlap constant \(C\) and experiment \(M\), the latent stationary overlap condition holds when \(C\ge 1\) and, writing \(d_e\) and \(d_b\) for the stationary laws of the target-policy and behavior-policy joint-state transition kernels, respectively,
\[
d_e(s)\le C\,d_b(s),
\qquad s\in\mathcal S .
\]

blocks.title: Observable trajectory space
blocks.body:
For a horizon \(T\) and observed-state cardinality \(n_X\), define the observable trajectory space \(\mathsf O_T\) by
\[
\mathsf O_T
=
\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\to
\bigl(\{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R\bigr).
\]
Thus an element of \(\mathsf O_T\) records, at each epoch \(t<T\), the observed coordinate \(X_t\), the binary action \(A_t\), and the real reward \(Y_t\). Equivalently, it is the sequence \(((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1}\).

blocks.title: Model-class assumption predicates
blocks.body:
For an observable-data POMDP experiment \((\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\) with \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), policy-induced kernels \(P_p\), stationary laws \(d_p\), \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\), and \(L=\exp(\zeta)\), write
\[
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{pomdp}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{ign}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{start}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{reward}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{act}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{mix}},\quad
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{stat}}
\]
for the following seven restrictions, respectively:
\[
\mathcal L(Y_t,X_{t+1},H_{t+1}\mid X_{0:t},H_{0:t},A_{0:t},Y_{0:t-1})
=
K(\cdot\mid X_t,H_t,A_t),
\qquad t=0,\ldots,T-1,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel};
\[
\Pr(A_t=a\mid X_{0:t},H_{0:t},A_{0:t-1},Y_{0:t-1})
=
b(a\mid X_t),
\qquad (a,t)\in\mathcal A\times\{0,\ldots,T-1\},
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability};
\[
S_0\sim d_b,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:stationary-start};
\[
\Pr(|Y_t|\le1)=1,
\qquad t=0,\ldots,T-1,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-reward};
\[
e(a\mid x)\le L b(a\mid x),
\qquad (a,x)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal X,
\qquad e\text{ a probability vector at each }x,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap};
\[
\|\nu P_p-\nu'P_p\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le
\alpha\|\nu-\nu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}},
\qquad (p,\nu,\nu')\in\{b,e\}\times\Delta(\mathcal S)^2,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:uniform-contraction}; and
\[
d_e(s)\le C d_b(s),
\qquad s\in\mathcal S,
\]
as in \cref{obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap}.

blocks.title: Latent-overlap POMDP class
blocks.body:
For \(T\in\mathbb N\) and \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is the class of all observable-data POMDP experiments
\[
(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))
\]
with the following defining properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Horizon and alphabets.)} The trajectory horizon satisfies \(1\le T\), the observed and latent alphabets \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal H\) are finite, and \(|\mathcal A|=2\).
\item \textbf{(Parameter scales.)} The mixing and log-overlap parameters satisfy \(0<t_0\) and \(0<\zeta\).
\item \textbf{(Raw experiment.)} The tuple has a reward-transition kernel \(K\), behavior policy \(b\), target policy \(e\), and probability law \(\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T)\) for the observed trajectory generated from the joint state coordinates \((X_t,H_t)\).
\item \textbf{(Seven restrictions.)} The seven restrictions in \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel,obj:ass:sequential-ignorability,obj:ass:stationary-start,obj:ass:bounded-reward,obj:ass:policy-overlap,obj:ass:uniform-contraction,obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap} hold, with policy-overlap factor \(L=\exp(\zeta)\) and contraction factor \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
:=
\left\{
(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T)):
\begin{array}{l}
1\le T,\quad |\mathcal X|<\infty,\quad |\mathcal H|<\infty,\quad |\mathcal A|=2,\\
0<t_0,\quad 0<\zeta,\\
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{pomdp}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{ign}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{start}},
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{reward}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{act}},
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{mix}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{stat}}\text{ hold}
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The class ranges over all finite observed and latent cardinalities and all revealed behavior-target policy pairs satisfying these conditions.

blocks.title: Target reward regression
blocks.body:
For any raw finite-state experiment \(M\) with target policy \(e\) and one-step law \(K\), and for every joint state \(s=(x,h)\in \{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{0,\ldots,n_H-1\}\), define the target-policy reward regression \(g_e\) by
\[
g_e(s)
=
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} e(a\mid x)\int r\,K(d r,d s'\mid s,a).
\]

blocks.title: Target value \(\theta(K,e)\)
blocks.body:
For the joint state \(S_t\) and the target-policy reward regression \(g_e\),
\[
\theta(K,e)
:=
\sum_{s=(x,h)\in\mathcal S} d_e(s)g_e(s)
=
\sum_{s=(x,h)\in\mathcal S} d_e(s)
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
e(a\mid x)\,E_K[Y_t\mid S_t=s,A_t=a].
\]

blocks.title: Estimator-specific risk
blocks.body:
Let
\[
M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))
\in \mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
\]
be a model in the latent-overlap class of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, whose observed trajectory is
\[
\mathsf O_T=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1},
\]
and let \(\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M\) denote the probability law of \(\mathsf O_T\) induced by \(M\) under the behavior policy \(b\).

For any observable-data estimator \(\widehat\theta\), its estimator-specific worst-case squared risk over \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta)
:=
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
\mathbb E_{\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M}
\!\left[
\left\{\widehat\theta(n_X,b,e,\mathsf O_T)-\theta(K,e)\right\}^2
\right],
\]
where \(n_X=|\mathcal X|\) is the revealed observed-alphabet size of \(M\). In particular,
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta_{k_T})
\]
is this quantity evaluated at the clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimator \(\widehat\theta_{k_T}\) with balanced history depth \(k_T\).

blocks.title: Observable minimax risk
blocks.body:
For a trajectory horizon \(T\ge 1\) and parameters \(t_0,\zeta,C\), the cardinality-uniform observable-data minimax squared-error risk is
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\theta}
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
\mathbb E_{\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M}
\!\left[
\left\{\widehat\theta(n_X,b,e,\mathsf O_T)-\theta(K,e)\right\}^2
\right].
\]
Here \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is the finite observed- and latent-state model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with unrestricted finite observed alphabet size \(n_X\) and unrestricted finite latent alphabet size, and \(\theta(K,e)\) is the stationary target-policy mean reward in \cref{obj:def:target-value}. The positive-horizon requirement \(1\le T\) is part of membership in \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), not a separate restriction on the supremum; at the degenerate horizon \(T=0\) the class is empty and the display is not used. The infimum ranges over all observable-data estimators \(\widehat\theta\) that take as inputs only \(n_X\), \(b\), \(e\), and the observed trajectory view \(\mathsf O_T\), are measurable in \(\mathsf O_T\) for each \(n_X,b,e\), and are uniformly valued in \([-1,1]\).

blocks.title: One-step policy ratio
blocks.body:
For behavior and target policy functions \(b,e : \{0,\ldots,n_X-1\}\times\{0,1\}\to\mathbb R\), the observable one-step policy ratio is
\[
\rho_t
=
\begin{cases}
0, & b(X_t,A_t)=0,\\
e(X_t,A_t)/b(X_t,A_t), & b(X_t,A_t)\ne 0.
\end{cases}
\]

blocks.title: Partial-history estimator \(\widehat\theta_k\)
blocks.body:
For \(0\le k<T\), define
\[
Z_t(k)
:=
Y_t\prod_{j=t-k}^{t}\rho_j,
\]
where \(\rho_t\) is the observable one-step policy ratio with the zero-cell convention. The clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimator is
\[
\widehat\theta_k
:=
\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
\left\{
\frac{1}{T-k}\sum_{t=k}^{T-1} Z_t(k)
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: History depth \(k_T\)
blocks.body:
For the contraction parameter \(\alpha\) and policy-overlap constant \(L\), the balanced fixed-radius history depth is
\[
k_T
:=
\min\left\{
\left\lfloor\frac{T}{2}\right\rfloor,
\max\left\{
0,
\left\lfloor
\frac{\log(T)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}
\right\rfloor
\right\}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Signed-depth family
blocks.body:
For a trajectory length \(T\), parameters \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), a terminal depth \(Q\in\mathbb N\), and an alternative index \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the signed-depth family is defined under
\[
t_0>0,\qquad \zeta>0,\qquad C>1,\qquad Q\ge 1.
\]
It is the raw POMDP experiment in \(\mathsf O_T\) with one observed state and \(2(Q+1)\) hidden states obtained by embedding the following finite-reward model.  The observed coordinate \(X_t\) is constant, and the hidden coordinate is written
\[
H_t=(J_t,U_t)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}.
\]
Writing \(\alpha\) for the mixing value determined by \(t_0\), \(L\) for the policy factor determined by \(\zeta\), \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\), and \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\), the behavior and target policies are
\[
b(A_t=1)=\frac{1}{L},\qquad b(A_t=0)=1-\frac{1}{L},
\qquad
e(A_t=1)=1,\qquad e(A_t=0)=0.
\]
The initial hidden-state law is the probability measure obtained from the weights
\[
w_j\frac{1+u\varepsilon_C L^{-j}}{2},
\qquad
w_j=
\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha^j}{1-\alpha^{Q+1}},
\qquad
j\in\{0,\ldots,Q\},\ u\in\{-1,+1\}.
\]
The transition kernel is the probability measure on reward-symbol and next-hidden-state pairs whose real weight at \((y,H_{t+1})\), with \(y\in\{-1,+1\}\), is the product of the reward weight
\[
\frac{1+yvc_0U_t\mathbf 1\{J_t=Q\}}{2}
\]
and the hidden-transition weight specified as follows.  A reset sign \(u'\) has weight
\[
\frac{1+u'\varepsilon_C}{2}.
\]
If \(J_t=Q\), then only transitions with \(J_{t+1}=0\) receive this reset-sign weight.  If \(J_t<Q\), transitions with \(J_{t+1}=0\) receive weight \((1-\alpha)(1+U_{t+1}\varepsilon_C)/2\), while transitions with \(J_{t+1}=J_t+1\) receive weight
\[
\alpha\,\mathbf 1\{U_{t+1}=U_t\}
\quad\text{when }A_t=1,
\qquad
\frac{\alpha}{2}
\quad\text{when }A_t=0,
\]
and all other hidden transitions receive weight zero.  The finite reward symbols are mapped to real rewards by \(0\mapsto -1\) and \(1\mapsto 1\), and the trajectory law is the finite chronological law generated by this initial distribution, behavior policy, and kernel, then embedded into the unrestricted real-reward raw experiment.

blocks.title: Overlap-distance radius \(q_C\)
blocks.body:
For \(C\ge 1\), define
\[
q_C:=\frac{C-1}{C}.
\]

blocks.title: Radius-calibrated history depth \(\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)\)
blocks.body:
For \(T\in\mathbb N\) and \(C\ge 1\), define
\[
\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C):=
\begin{cases}
0, & Tq_C^2\le 1,\\[3pt]
\displaystyle
\min\!\left\{
\left\lfloor\frac T2\right\rfloor,
\left\lfloor\frac{\log(Tq_C^2)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor
\right\},
& Tq_C^2>1.
\end{cases}
\]

blocks.title: Finite signed-depth observed-word law
blocks.body:
For \(C>1\), \(Q\ge1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let
\[
\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{fin},T}
\]
be the finite observed-word law through horizon \(T\) generated by the signed-depth construction of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}. Its observed state is constant, its latent state is \(H_t=(J_t,U_t)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}\), its behavior and target policies satisfy \(b(1)=1/L\) and \(e(1)=1\), and its reward alphabet is \(\{-1,+1\}\) with
\[
\Pr_v(Y_t=y\mid J_t,U_t,A_t)
=
\frac{1+yvc_0U_t\mathbf 1\{J_t=Q\}}{2}.
\]
The initial latent law is \(d_b(j,u)=w_j(1+u\varepsilon_C L^{-j})/2\), and the resulting finite observation consists of the action-reward word \((A_t,Y_t)_{t=0}^{T-1}\), equivalently the finite observed trajectory with constant observed-state coordinate.

blocks.title: Target value of an indexed model
blocks.body:
For an indexed model \(m\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), write \(K_m\) and \(e_m\) for its joint reward-transition kernel and target policy. The target value of \(m\) is
\[
\theta_m:=\theta(K_m,e_m),
\]
with \(\theta(K,e)\) the stationary target-policy causal value from \(\cref{obj:def:target-value}\).

blocks.title: Unclipped partial-history average
blocks.body:
For the balanced history depth \(k_T\), define the unclipped partial-history average by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\rm raw}_{k_T}
:=
\frac{1}{T-k_T}\sum_{t=k_T}^{T-1} Z_t(k_T),
\qquad
Z_t(k_T):=
Y_t\prod_{j=t-k_T}^{t}\rho_j .
\]
Here \(\rho_j=e(A_j\mid X_j)/b(A_j\mid X_j)\) on behavior-supported cells, with the zero-cell convention used for \(\rho_j\).

blocks.title: Uniform overlap frontier
blocks.body:
Fix \(t_0>0\) and \(\zeta>0\).  Let \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) be the minimax squared-error risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, let \(q_C=(C-1)/C\) be the overlap-distance radius in \cref{obj:def:overlap-distance-radius}, and set
\[
\beta=\frac{2}{2+t_0\zeta},
\qquad
\mathfrak r_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
=
T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)} .
\]
There exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}}>0\), with
\(c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\), and an integer \(T_\star\ge 1\), all depending only on \(t_0\) and \(\zeta\), such that for every \(C\ge 1\) and every \(T\ge T_\star\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{lo}}\mathfrak r_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
\le
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
\le
c_{\mathrm{hi}}\mathfrak r_T(t_0,\zeta,C),
\]
and the radius-adaptive partial-history importance-weighted estimator with depth
\(\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)\) from \cref{obj:def:radius-adaptive-history-depth} satisfies
\[
\sup_{m\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
\mathbb E_m\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)}-\theta_m\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
c_{\mathrm{hi}}\mathfrak r_T(t_0,\zeta,C).
\]
Moreover, for every sequence \(C_T\ge 1\), if \(Tq_{C_T}^2\) is eventually bounded, then there is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{imm}}>0\), depending on the sequence and on \(t_0,\zeta\), such that eventually
\[
\sup_{m\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C_T)}
\mathbb E_m\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\theta_{0}-\theta_m\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{c_{\mathrm{imm}}}{T}.
\]

blocks.title: Fixed-overlap minimax rate
blocks.body:
Fix \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive memory exponent.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap exponent.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed latent-overlap radius.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
Let the exponent \(\beta\) be
\[
\beta=\frac{2}{2+t_0\zeta}.
\]
There exist constants \(c_\star,c^\star\in\mathbb R\) and an integer \(T_\star\ge 1\) such that
\[
0<c_\star\le c^\star
\]
and, for every integer \(T\ge T_\star\),
\[
c_\star T^{-\beta}
\le
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
\le
c^\star T^{-\beta},
\]
where \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is the minimax squared-error risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}. Moreover, the clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimator \(\widehat\theta_{k_T}\), with \(k_T\) as in \cref{obj:def:history-depth}, satisfies
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
\mathbb E_M\!\left[
\{\widehat\theta_{k_T}-\theta(M)\}^2
\right]
\le
c^\star T^{-\beta},
\]
with \(\theta(M)\) the stationary target-policy mean reward in \cref{obj:def:target-value}.

For each integer \(T\ge T_\star\), there is an integer \(Q\ge 1\) such that the lower bound is witnessed by the two signed-depth alternatives \(M_{Q,v}^T\), \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), generated by \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} with one observed state and \(2(Q+1)\) latent states: for every measurable observable-data estimator \(\widehat\theta\), under the usual squared-error integrability conditions for both alternatives,
\[
c_\star T^{-\beta}
\le
\max_{v\in\{-1,+1\}}
\mathbb E_{M_{Q,v}^T}\!\left[
\{\widehat\theta-\theta(M_{Q,v}^T)\}^2
\right].
\]

blocks.title: Unit overlap boundary
blocks.body:
Let \(t_0>0\) and \(\zeta>0\). At unit latent overlap, \(C=1\), the following assertions hold.

For every trajectory length \(T\), every finite observed and hidden state cardinalities, and every experiment \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,1)\) in the model class of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, the target stationary law \(d_e\) and the behavior stationary law \(d_b\) of the corresponding policy-induced joint-state transition kernels coincide:
\[
d_e=d_b .
\]

Moreover, there is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{imm}}>0\), depending only on \(t_0\) and \(\zeta\), such that for every integer \(T\ge 1\), the worst-case squared risk of the immediate observable estimator \(\widehat\theta_0\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,1)}
\mathbb E_M\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\theta_0-\theta(K,e)\bigr)^2\right]
\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{imm}}}{T}.
\]
Finally, for the minimax squared-error risk \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,1)\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, there are constants \(c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}}>0\) with \(c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\) and an integer \(T_\star\ge 1\) such that, for every \(T\ge T_\star\),
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{lo}}}{T}
\le
R_T(t_0,\zeta,1)
\le
\frac{c_{\mathrm{hi}}}{T}.
\]
The hidden-state exponent at these positive scales satisfies
\[
\frac{2}{2+t_0\zeta}<1 .
\]

blocks.title: Shrinking-overlap frontier
blocks.body:
The following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Fixed smoothness.)} The constants satisfy \(t_0>0\) and \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Shrinking radius.)} The deterministic radius excess sequence \((\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\) satisfies \(\delta_T\ge0\) for every \(T\).
\item \textbf{(Local limit.)} The sequence satisfies \(\delta_T\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Rate exponent.)} Let \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\).
\item \textbf{(Local rate and depth.)} Define
\[
r_T(\delta)
=
T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}
\]
and
\[
\kappa_T
=
\begin{cases}
0, & T\delta_T^2\le 1,\\[3pt]
\displaystyle
\min\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
\left\lfloor
\frac{\log(T\delta_T^2)}
{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}
\right\rfloor\right\}, & T\delta_T^2>1.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{loc}},C_{\mathrm{loc}}\) with
\(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}\le C_{\mathrm{loc}}\), depending only on \(t_0\) and
\(\zeta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{loc}}\,r_T(\delta)
\le
R_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)
\le
C_{\mathrm{loc}}\,r_T(\delta),
\]
where \(R_T\) is the minimax squared-error risk in
\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.  Moreover, the observable partial-history
importance-weighted estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T}\) of
\cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator} satisfies
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)}
\mathbb E_M\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T}-\theta(M)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\mathrm{loc}}\,r_T(\delta)
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Finally, if there is a constant \(D\ge0\)
such that \(T\delta_T^2\le D\) for all sufficiently large \(T\), then there is
a constant \(c_{\mathrm{imm}}>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)}
\mathbb E_M\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{0}-\theta(M)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{c_{\mathrm{imm}}}{T}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).

blocks.title: Insulin grid \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\)
blocks.body:
The finite insulin-grid state is
\[
s=(g,d_1,d_2,x_1,x_2,a_1)
\in
\{50,100,150,200,250\}
\times\{0,78\}^2
\times\{0,31,850\}^2
\times\{0,1\},
\]
so the state space has \(360\) states. The diet coordinates form
\[
H_t=(d_1,d_2),
\]
and all other coordinates form \(X_t\). The behavior and target policies are
\[
b(1\mid X_t)=0.3,
\qquad
e(1\mid X_t)=\mathbf 1\{g\ge 125\}.
\]
With probability \(1/2\), the next full state is drawn uniformly. With the remaining probability, draw
\[
d_0\in\{0,78\}
\quad\text{with probabilities}\quad
(0.8,0.2),
\]
draw
\[
x_0\in\{0,31,850\}
\quad\text{with probabilities}\quad
(0.4,0.4,0.2),
\]
draw \(\xi\sim N(0,25)\), and set
\[
g'
=
\operatorname{round}_{\{50,100,150,200,250\}}
\operatorname{clip}_{[50,250]}
\bigl(
10+0.9g+0.1d_1+0.1d_2-0.01x_1-0.01x_2-2A_t-4a_1+\xi
\bigr).
\]
The memory coordinates then shift to
\[
(g',d_0,d_1,x_0,x_1,A_t).
\]
The reward is
\[
Y_t=
\begin{cases}
-1, & g\le 70,\\
-2/3, & g>150,\\
-1/3, & 70<g\le 80\ \text{or}\ 120<g\le 150,\\
0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
This construction defines \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\).

blocks.title: Uniform one-half contraction of the insulin-grid policy kernels
blocks.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\) and let \(p\) assign to each of the \(90\) observed states of the refreshed finite insulin adaptation \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\) of \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid} a probability law on the action set \(\{0,1\}\). Write \(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}\) for the \(360\)-point joint state space, \(x(s)\) for the observed coordinate of a grid state \(s\), \(K_T\) for the transition kernel of \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\), and
\[
P_p^{(T)}(s,s')=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}p(a\mid x(s))\,K_T\{(q,s''):\ s''=s'\mid s,a\},
\qquad s,s'\in\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}},
\]
for the induced transition matrix. Then, for all probability vectors \(\nu,\nu'\) on \(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}\),
\[
\|\nu P_p^{(T)}-\nu'P_p^{(T)}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le
\frac12\|\nu-\nu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}} ,
\]
equivalently, in the \(\ell^1\) norm \(\|\cdot\|_1=2\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
\|\nu P_p^{(T)}-\nu'P_p^{(T)}\|_1\le\frac12\|\nu-\nu'\|_1 .
\]

blocks.title: The selected insulin-grid stationary law is stationary
blocks.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\) and let \(p\) assign to each observed state of the refreshed finite insulin adaptation \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\) of \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid} a probability law on \(\{0,1\}\). Suppose that the induced transition matrix \(P_p^{(T)}\) on the joint state space \(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}\) satisfies
\[
\|\nu P_p^{(T)}-\nu'P_p^{(T)}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\frac12\|\nu-\nu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\]
for all probability vectors \(\nu,\nu'\) on \(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}\). Then the stationary law \(d_p\) selected for \(P_p^{(T)}\) is a probability vector and satisfies the stationarity equations
\[
d_p(s')=\sum_{s\in\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}}d_p(s)P_p^{(T)}(s,s'),
\qquad s'\in\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}} .
\]

blocks.title: Target-policy reward regression on the insulin grid
blocks.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\) be the refreshed finite insulin adaptation of \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid} with transition kernel \(K_T\) and target policy \(e\), and for a grid state \(s=(g,d_1,d_2,x_1,x_2,a_1)\) write \(x(s)=(g,x_1,x_2,a_1)\) for its observed coordinate and
\[
r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s)=
\begin{cases}
-1,&g\le70,\\
-2/3,&g>150,\\
-1/3,&70<g\le80\ \text{or}\ 120<g\le150,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
for the insulin reward vector. Writing \(p_1\) for the numeric reward coordinate of a reward/state pair \(p\) drawn by \(K_T\), we have, for every \(s\in\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}\),
\[
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}e(a\mid x(s))\int p_1\,K_T(dp\mid s,a)
=
r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s) .
\]

blocks.title: Immediate weighted reward regression on the insulin grid
blocks.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\) be the refreshed finite insulin adaptation of \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid} with transition kernel \(K_T\), behavior policy \(b\) and target policy \(e\), and for a grid state \(s=(g,d_1,d_2,x_1,x_2,a_1)\) write \(x(s)=(g,x_1,x_2,a_1)\). Let
\[
\rho(x,a)=\begin{cases}e(a\mid x)/b(a\mid x),&b(a\mid x)\ne0,\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}
\]
and let \(r_{\mathrm{ins}}\) be the insulin reward vector
\[
r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s)=
\begin{cases}
-1,&g\le70,\\
-2/3,&g>150,\\
-1/3,&70<g\le80\ \text{or}\ 120<g\le150,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
Writing \(p_1\) for the numeric reward coordinate of a reward/state pair \(p\) drawn by \(K_T\), we have, for every \(s\in\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}\),
\[
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}b(a\mid x(s))\,\rho(x(s),a)\int p_1\,K_T(dp\mid s,a)
=
r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s) .
\]

blocks.title: Stationary reward enclosure
blocks.body:
Let \(\mathsf S\) be a finite set, and let \(P\) be a stochastic matrix on \(\mathsf S\) whose entries satisfy
\[
P(s,s')\in\mathfrak A(s,s')
\]
for all \(s,s'\in\mathsf S\). The intervals are rational intervals \([\ell,u]\) with \(\ell\le u\), combined by exact interval arithmetic:
\[
[a,b]+[c,d]=[a+c,b+d],\qquad
[a,b]\ominus[c,d]=[a-d,b-c],
\]
and \([a,b]\cdot[c,d]\) is the interval whose endpoints are the smallest and largest of the four endpoint products. For an interval \(\mathfrak r\), write \(\ell(\mathfrak r)\) and \(u(\mathfrak r)\) for its endpoints and
\[
|\mathfrak r|_{\max}=\max\{|\ell(\mathfrak r)|,|u(\mathfrak r)|\}.
\]
Suppose the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Initial row and interval rows.)} There are an exact rational probability vector \(\mu_0\) on \(\mathsf S\), a number \(m\in\mathbb N\), and interval rows \(\mathfrak T_0,\ldots,\mathfrak T_{m+1}\) on \(\mathsf S\) such that
\[
\mu_0(s)\in\mathfrak T_0(s)
\]
for every \(s\in\mathsf S\).

\item \textbf{(Chunked recurrence.)} For every \(k\le m\) and every output state \(s'\), there are pairwise disjoint blocks \(\mathcal G_1,\ldots,\mathcal G_J\subseteq\mathsf S\) covering \(\mathsf S\), each with at most a fixed positive number of states; block intervals \(\Xi_1(s'),\ldots,\Xi_J(s')\); and partial-sum intervals \(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{J+1}\) such that
\[
\sum_{s\in\mathcal G_j}\mathfrak T_k(s)\cdot\mathfrak A(s,s')\subseteq\Xi_j(s')
\]
for each \(j\),
\[
0\in\Sigma_{J+1},\qquad
\Xi_j(s')+\Sigma_{j+1}\subseteq\Sigma_j
\]
for \(j=J,\ldots,1\), and
\[
\Sigma_1=\mathfrak T_{k+1}(s').
\]

\item \textbf{(Reward bounds.)} There are a reward vector \(r:\mathsf S\to\mathbb R\), rational intervals \(\mathfrak r(s)\ni r(s)\), and a rational bound \(B\ge0\) such that
\[
|\mathfrak r(s)|_{\max}\le B
\]
for every \(s\in\mathsf S\).

\item \textbf{(Contraction and stationarity.)} There are a rational coefficient \(0\le\rho<1\) and a probability vector \(\pi\) such that
\[
\|\nu P-\nu'P\|_1\le\rho\|\nu-\nu'\|_1
\]
for all probability vectors \(\nu,\nu'\) on \(\mathsf S\), and
\[
\pi P=\pi .
\]
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
\delta=\sum_{s\in\mathsf S}\bigl|\mathfrak T_m(s)\ominus\mathfrak T_{m+1}(s)\bigr|_{\max},
\qquad
\mathfrak E=\sum_{s\in\mathsf S}\mathfrak T_m(s)\cdot\mathfrak r(s),
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak J=
\left[
\ell(\mathfrak E)-\frac{B\delta}{1-\rho},
u(\mathfrak E)+\frac{B\delta}{1-\rho}
\right].
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{s\in\mathsf S}\pi(s)\,r(s)\in\mathfrak J .
\]

blocks.title: Insulin bias interval bounds
blocks.body:
For \(\star\in\{\mathrm b,\mathrm e\}\), let \(\mathfrak T_{\star,0}\) and \(\mathfrak T_{\star,1}\) be the terminal and successor rational interval rows on the \(360\)-state grid \(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}\) of \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid} recorded by the zero-step chunked iterate certificate, in blocks of at most \(40\) states, for the rational interval enclosure of the behavior-policy case \(\star=\mathrm b\) or target-policy case \(\star=\mathrm e\). Let \(\mathfrak r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s)=[r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s),r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s)]\), where \(r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s)\in\{-1,-2/3,-1/3,0\}\) is the grid reward from \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid}. Using the exact rational interval arithmetic of \cref{obj:lem:certified-stationary-reward-enclosure}, define
\[
\delta_\star=\sum_{s\in\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}}\bigl|\mathfrak T_{\star,0}(s)\ominus\mathfrak T_{\star,1}(s)\bigr|_{\max},
\qquad
\mathfrak E_\star=\sum_{s\in\mathsf S_{\mathrm{grid}}}\mathfrak T_{\star,0}(s)\cdot\mathfrak r_{\mathrm{ins}}(s),
\]
\[
\mathfrak J_\star=
\left[
\ell(\mathfrak E_\star)-\frac{\delta_\star}{1-1/2},
\,
u(\mathfrak E_\star)+\frac{\delta_\star}{1-1/2}
\right],
\qquad
\mathfrak B=\mathfrak J_{\mathrm b}\ominus\mathfrak J_{\mathrm e}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\mathfrak B=
\left[
\ell(\mathfrak J_{\mathrm b})-u(\mathfrak J_{\mathrm e}),
\,
u(\mathfrak J_{\mathrm b})-\ell(\mathfrak J_{\mathrm e})
\right].
\]
Then the endpoints of this rational interval satisfy
\[
-\frac{6}{1000}<\ell(\mathfrak B)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
u(\mathfrak B)<-\frac{58}{10000}.
\]

blocks.title: Insulin-grid bias certificate
blocks.body:
For every natural horizon \(T\), let \(\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}(T)\) be the stationary immediate-weighting bias for the refreshed finite insulin adaptation \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\) of \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid},
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}(T)
=
\sum_s d_b(s)
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}
b(s_1,a)\,
\rho(s_1,a)\,
\int p_1\,K_T(dp\mid s,a)
-
\theta(K_T,e),
\]
where \(d_b\) is the stationary law of the behavior-policy transition kernel on the insulin grid, \(K_T\) is the refreshed insulin-grid transition kernel, \(b\) and \(e\) are its behavior and target policies, \(\rho(s_1,a)\) is the one-step target-to-behavior policy ratio, and \(\theta(K_T,e)\) is the target value in \cref{obj:def:target-value}. Then
\[
-\frac{6}{1000}
<
\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}(T)
<
-\frac{58}{10000}.
\]

blocks.title: Finite insulin witness
blocks.body:
For every horizon \(T\), the refreshed insulin experiment \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\) of \cref{obj:def:insulin-grid} satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(State count.)} Its observed--latent joint-state alphabet has cardinality \(90\cdot 4=360\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform contraction.)} It satisfies \cref{obj:ass:uniform-contraction} with contraction parameter \(\alpha=1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Policy overlap.)} It satisfies \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap} with one-step overlap constant \(L=10/3\).
\item \textbf{(Stationary overlap.)} It satisfies \cref{obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap} with stationary-overlap constant \(C=720\).
\end{itemize}
Define the immediate-weighting bias diagnostic by
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}(T)
=
\sum_s d_b(s)\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} b(a\mid s_X)\,
\frac{e(a\mid s_X)}{b(a\mid s_X)}
\int r\,K(ds',dr\mid s,a)
-
\theta(K,e),
\]
where \(K,b,e\) are the transition kernel, behavior policy, and target policy of \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\), \(s_X\) is the observed coordinate of \(s\), and \(d_b\) is the stationary law induced by \(b\). This diagnostic is interval-certified as strictly negative:
\[
-0.006 < \Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}(T) < -0.0058 .
\]

blocks.title: Filter quantities \(\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}},\ell_t,q_t^v,a_t^{(Q)}\)
blocks.body:
Define
\[
\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}
:=
\sigma(A_0,Y_0,\ldots,A_{t-1},Y_{t-1}),
\]
\[
\ell_t:=\min\{Q,t\},
\]
\[
q_t^v
:=
\Pr_v(J_t=Q\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}),
\]
and
\[
a_t^{(Q)}
:=
L^{-(Q-\ell_t)}
\prod_{j=t-\ell_t}^{t-1}\mathbf 1\{A_j=1\},
\]
where the empty product is equal to one.

blocks.title: Window second moment
blocks.body:
Let \(T,n_X,n_H\in\mathbb N\), let \(k\in\mathbb N\), let \(L\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M\) be a raw POMDP experiment on finite observed and hidden alphabets. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sequential ignorability.)} \(M\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability}.
\item \textbf{(Policy overlap.)} \(M\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap} with constant \(L\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} \(L\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Kernel law.)} \(M\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel}.
\item \textbf{(Bounded rewards.)} \(M\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:bounded-reward}.
\item \textbf{(Window position.)} \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\) and \(k\le t\).
\end{itemize}
For the depth-\(k\) score \(Z_t(k)\) of \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}, under the observed trajectory law of \(M\),
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathrm{obs}}\bigl[Z_t(k)^2\bigr]\le L^{k+1}.
\]

blocks.title: Overlapping-window covariance
blocks.body:
Let \(M\) be a raw POMDP experiment of length \(T\) on finite observed and hidden alphabets. Let \(k,h\in\mathbb N\), let \(L\in\mathbb R\), and let \(t,u\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model conditions.)} \(M\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability}, \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap} with overlap constant \(L\), \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel}, and \cref{obj:ass:bounded-reward}.
\item \textbf{(Overlap constant.)} \(L\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Initial window.)} \(k\le t\).
\item \textbf{(Lag identity.)} \(u=t+h\).
\item \textbf{(Overlapping lag.)} \(1\le h\le k\).
\end{itemize}
Then the depth-\(k\) scores \(Z_t(k)\) of \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}, evaluated under the observed trajectory law of \(M\), satisfy
\[
\bigl|\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{obs}}\bigl(Z_t(k),Z_u(k)\bigr)\bigr|
\le
2L^{k+1-h}.
\]

blocks.title: Observed-trajectory law
blocks.body:
For a raw POMDP experiment \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\), let
\[
\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M
\]
denote the probability law of the observed trajectory
\[
\mathsf O_T=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1}
\]
induced by the behavior-policy experiment \(M\). Equivalently, under \(\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(S_0\sim d_b\), \(A_t\sim b(\cdot\mid X_t)\), and \(K\) generates \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), with only \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)_{t=0}^{T-1}\) retained.

blocks.title: Full trajectory law and observation map
blocks.body:
For a raw POMDP experiment \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\) with joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\), let \(\mathbb P_M\) denote the full behavior-policy trajectory law on
\[
(S_0,A_0,Y_0,S_1,\ldots,A_{T-1},Y_{T-1},S_T).
\]
Under \(\mathbb P_M\), the initial state satisfies \(S_0\sim d_b\), each action is drawn as \(A_t\sim b(\cdot\mid X_t)\), and the kernel \(K\) generates \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), for \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\).

Let \(O\) be the observation map from a full trajectory to its observed trajectory,
\[
O(S_0,A_0,Y_0,\ldots,A_{T-1},Y_{T-1},S_T)
:=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=0}^{T-1},
\]
where \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\). The observed behavior-policy law is the pushforward
\[
\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\mathbb P_M\circ O^{-1}.
\]

blocks.title: Separated window peeling
blocks.body:
Let \(M\) be a raw POMDP experiment with trajectory length \(T\), and let \(L\), the policy-overlap constant, be real. Let \(Z_s(k)\) denote the depth-\(k\) partial-history weighted reward score from \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model conditions.)} \(M\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability,obj:ass:policy-overlap,obj:ass:pomdp-kernel,obj:ass:bounded-reward} with overlap constant \(L\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap scale.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Mature earlier window.)} The history depth \(k\) satisfies \(k\le t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated future window.)} For an epoch \(t\) and a gap \(\gamma\in\mathbb N\), the epoch
\[
u=t+1+\gamma+k
\]
lies in the observed horizon, equivalently \(t+1+\gamma+k<T\).
\end{itemize}
For \(p\in\{b,e\}\), let \(P_p\) be the policy-induced transition operator obtained from the reward-marginalized kernel under policy \(p\), let
\[
g_e(s)=\sum_a e(a\mid x(s))\int y\,K(dy\times\mathcal S\mid s,a),
\]
and put
\[
\Phi_{\gamma,k}(s)=P_b^\gamma P_e^k g_e(s).
\]
Then, with \(\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}\) the observed law induced by the observed trajectory map \(O\),
\[
\int Z_t(k)(w)Z_u(k)(w)\,d\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}(w)
=
\int Z_t(k)(O(\tau))\,\Phi_{\gamma,k}(S_{t+1}(\tau))\,d\mathbb P_M(\tau).
\]

blocks.title: Behavior-support operator congruence
blocks.body:
Let \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) satisfy \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with behavior policy \(b\), target policy \(e\), and the policy-overlap condition in \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap}.  For \(p\in\{b,e\}\), write
\[
P_p(s,s')=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} p(a\mid x(s))\,K(\{S'=s'\}\mid s,a),
\]
and let \(P_p^0 h=h\) and \(P_p^{m+1}h=P_p(P_p^m h)\).  Let \(d_b\) denote the behavior stationary law of \(P_b\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Policy choice.)} The policy \(p\) is either \(b\) or \(e\).
\item \textbf{(Terminal agreement.)} The functions \(f,g:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[
f(s)=g(s)
\]
for every joint state \(s\) with \(d_b(s)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Initial support.)} The joint state \(s\) satisfies \(d_b(s)>0\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(m\in\mathbb N\),
\[
(P_p^m f)(s)=(P_p^m g)(s).
\]

blocks.title: Separated window covariance
blocks.body:
Let \(T,n_X,n_H,k,h\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) be a raw POMDP experiment as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with the uniform contraction restriction of \cref{obj:ass:uniform-contraction}. Write the contraction factor as \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\). Let \(t,u\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\) satisfy
\[
k\le t,\qquad u=t+h,\qquad k+1\le h .
\]
Then the depth-\(k\) scores \(Z_t(k)\) of \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}, evaluated under the observed trajectory law of \(M\), satisfy
\[
\bigl|\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{obs}}\bigl(Z_t(k),Z_u(k)\bigr)\bigr|
\le
2\alpha^{h-k-1}.
\]

blocks.title: Aggregate future-covariance bound
blocks.body:
Let \(T\ge1\), \(k\in\mathbb N\), \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) be as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Write \(L=e^{\zeta}\), \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\), and \(\mathscr T_k=\{t:k\le t\le T-1\}\). Then, for every \(t\in\mathscr T_k\), the depth-\(k\) scores of \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator} satisfy, under the observed trajectory law of \(M\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{u\in\mathscr T_k\\ t<u}}
\bigl|\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{obs}}\bigl(Z_t(k),Z_u(k)\bigr)\bigr|
\le
\frac{2L^{k+1}}{L-1}+\frac{2}{1-\alpha}.
\]

blocks.title: Raw variance assembly
blocks.body:
Let \(T\) and \(k\) be nonnegative integers, let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M\) be a raw POMDP experiment. Write \(L=e^\zeta\) for the policy-overlap factor and \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\) for the contraction factor. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Horizon.)} \(T\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), with \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(History depth.)} \(k\le \lfloor T/2\rfloor\).
\end{itemize}
For the depth-\(k\) scores \(Z_t(k)\) of \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}, form the unclipped partial-history average
\[
\frac{1}{T-k}\sum_{t=k}^{T-1} Z_t(k).
\]
Under the observed trajectory law obtained by projecting the full trajectory law of \(M\) onto observed histories, its variance satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac{1}{T-k}\sum_{t=k}^{T-1} Z_t(k)\right)
\le
\frac{2}{T}\left\{
L^{k+1}\left(1+\frac{4}{L-1}\right)
+
\frac{4}{1-\alpha}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Balanced PHIW upper bound
blocks.body:
Fix constants satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Mixing scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Policy-overlap scale.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-overlap radius.)} \(C\ge 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(k_T\) be the balanced history depth in \cref{obj:def:history-depth}, and set
\[
\beta=\frac{2}{2+t_0\zeta}.
\]
Then there exist constants \(c^\star>0\) and \(T_\star\in\mathbb N\) such that, for every \(T\ge T_\star\), the estimator-specific worst-case squared risk from \cref{obj:synth_13} of the observable PHIW estimator \(\widehat\theta_{k_T}\) from \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator} satisfies
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta_{k_T})
\le
c^\star T^{-\beta}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(T\ge T_\star\), every finite alphabet sizes \(n_X,n_H\), and every raw POMDP experiment \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), the variance under the observed trajectory law induced by \(M\) of the unclipped partial-history average
\[
\frac{1}{T-k_T}\sum_{t=k_T}^{T-1} Z_t(k_T)
\]
satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}
\!\left(\frac{1}{T-k_T}\sum_{t=k_T}^{T-1} Z_t(k_T)\right)
\le
\frac{2}{T}
\left[
e^{\zeta(k_T+1)}
\left(1+\frac{4}{e^\zeta-1}\right)
+
\frac{4}{1-e^{-1/t_0}}
\right].
\]

blocks.title: Contraction of the constant-policy signed-depth kernel
blocks.body:
Let \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(C\ge1\), \(Q\ge1\), \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\) and \(r\in[0,1]\), and write \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\). Let \(P^{(r)}\) be the transition kernel induced on the joint state space \(\mathcal S_Q=\{0\}\times(\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\})\) of the signed-depth alternative of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} with terminal depth \(Q\) and index \(v\) by the constant policy \(a_r\) that plays action one with probability \(r\). Then, for all probability vectors \(\mu,\mu'\) on \(\mathcal S_Q\),
\[
\|\mu P^{(r)}-\mu'P^{(r)}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le
\alpha\|\mu-\mu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}} .
\]

blocks.title: Closed form of the signed-depth stationary law
blocks.body:
Let \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(C\ge1\), \(Q\ge1\), \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\) and \(r\in[0,1]\). Write \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\), \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\), and \(w_j=(1-\alpha)\alpha^{j}/(1-\alpha^{Q+1})\). Let \(P^{(r)}\) be the kernel induced on \(\mathcal S_Q\) by the constant policy \(a_r\) for the signed-depth alternative of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} with terminal depth \(Q\) and index \(v\), and let \(d_r\) be the stationary law selected for \(P^{(r)}\). Then, for every hidden state \(h=(j(h),u(h))\),
\[
d_r(0,h)
=
w_{j(h)}\,\frac{1+u(h)\varepsilon_Cr^{j(h)}}{2}.
\]

blocks.title: Signed-depth membership
blocks.body:
For every \(T\ge 1\), \(Q\ge 1\), \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(C>1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let \(M_{Q,v}^T\) be the signed-depth experiment of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}.  Put
\[
\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\},
\qquad
L=\exp(\zeta),
\qquad
w_j=\frac{(1-\alpha(t_0))\alpha(t_0)^j}{1-\alpha(t_0)^{Q+1}},
\]
where \(\alpha(t_0)\) is the mixing factor and \(j=0,\ldots,Q\).  Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Membership.)} \(M_{Q,v}^T\in \mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Behavior stationary law.)} For every hidden state \(h\), with decoded depth \(j(h)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\) and sign \(u(h)\in\{-1,+1\}\),
\[
d_b(0,h)
=
w_{j(h)}
\frac{1+u(h)\varepsilon_C L^{-j(h)}}{2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Constant action-one stationary laws.)} For every \(r\in[0,1]\), if \(d_r\) denotes the stationary law induced by the constant policy that chooses action one with probability \(r\), then for every hidden state \(h\),
\[
d_r(0,h)
=
w_{j(h)}
\frac{1+u(h)\varepsilon_C r^{j(h)}}{2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Target-over-behavior domination.)} For every joint state \(s\),
\[
d_e(s)\le (1+\varepsilon_C)d_b(s),
\qquad
1+\varepsilon_C\le C.
\]
\end{itemize}
The stationary target value of \cref{obj:def:target-value} is
\[
\theta(K,e)
=
v\,c_0(t_0)\,\varepsilon_C\,w_Q .
\]

blocks.title: Posterior window power bound
blocks.body:
Let \(N,Q,k,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C,b\in\mathbb R\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and let \(o=((a_0,y_0),\ldots,(a_{k-1},y_{k-1}))\) be an observed prefix for the signed-depth family of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}.  Write
\[
c_0(t_0)=\frac{1-\alpha(t_0)}{4},
\]
and, for \(0\le m\le k\), write \(o_{\le m}\) for the first \(m\) observed pairs.  For any observed prefix \(o'\), define the raw terminal-depth posterior by
\[
\pi_v(o')
=
\frac{\sum_h \mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\lambda_v(h;o')}
     {\sum_h \lambda_v(h;o')}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative amplitude.)} \(0\le c_0(t_0)\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative base.)} \(0\le 1-c_0(t_0)b\).
\item \textbf{(Window length.)} \(d\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Strict-prefix posterior bound.)} For every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\),
\[
\pi_v(o_{\le i})\le b.
\]
\end{itemize}
Define the final \(d\)-prefix lower window by
\[
\Lambda_d(o)
=
\prod_{\substack{0\le i<k\\ k-d\le i}}
\left(1-c_0(t_0)\pi_v(o_{\le i})\right).
\]
Then
\[
\bigl(1-c_0(t_0)b\bigr)^d\le \Lambda_d(o).
\]

blocks.title: Terminal posterior window bound
blocks.body:
Let \(N,Q\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\).  Put \(\alpha=\exp\{-(1/t_0)\}\).  In the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}, for an observed prefix \(o=((a_1,y_1),\ldots,(a_k,y_k))\), write
\[
\pi_v(o)
=
\frac{
\sum_{h\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}}
\mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\lambda_v(h;o)
}{
\mathsf M_v(o)
}.
\]
For \(d\in\mathbb N\), define the lower posterior window
\[
\Lambda_d(o)
=
\prod_{\substack{0\le i<k\\ k-d\le i}}
\left(1-c_0(t_0)\,\pi_v(o_{\le i})\right),
\]
where \(o_{\le i}\) is the prefix of \(o\) containing its first \(i\) action--reward pairs.

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive tilt.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} \(C>1\).
\item \textbf{(Mature window.)} \(Q\le k\).
\end{itemize}
Then the terminal-depth posterior satisfies
\[
\pi_v(o)
\le
\frac{\alpha^Q}{\Lambda_Q(o)}.
\]

blocks.title: Initial-window posterior bound
blocks.body:
Let \(N,Q\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let \(k\in\mathbb N\), and let
\[
o:\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to \{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}
\]
be an observed action/reward prefix for the signed-depth construction of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}.  Write \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\).  For any prefix \(o'\), define the raw terminal-depth posterior by
\[
\pi_v(o')
=
\frac{\sum_{h:\,J(h)=Q}\lambda_v(h;o')}
     {\sum_h \lambda_v(h;o')}.
\]
Define the initial lower posterior window over the available prefixes by
\[
\Lambda_k(o)
=
\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}
\left(1-c_0\,\pi_v(o_{\le i})\right),
\]
where \(o_{\le i}\) is the prefix of \(o\) of length \(i\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap exponent.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Nontrivial overlap radius.)} \(C>1\).
\item \textbf{(Initial window.)} \(k<Q\).
\end{itemize}
Then the terminal-depth posterior after observing \(o\) satisfies
\[
\pi_v(o)\le \frac{\alpha^Q}{\Lambda_k(o)}.
\]

blocks.title: Crude terminal posterior bound
blocks.body:
Let \(N,Q,k\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive temperature.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive log-overlap.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
For the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}, write
\[
\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0),
\qquad
c_0=\frac{1-\alpha}{4}.
\]
For every observed prefix \(o\in(\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\})^k\), define the raw terminal-depth posterior by
\[
\pi_v(o)
=
\frac{
\sum_h \mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\,\lambda_v(h;o)
}{
\mathsf M_v(o)
},
\qquad
\mathsf M_v(o)=\sum_h \lambda_v(h;o),
\]
where the sums range over the signed-depth hidden states at depth horizon \(Q\). Then
\[
\pi_v(o)
\le
\left(\frac{\alpha}{1-c_0}\right)^Q .
\]

blocks.title: Refined terminal posterior bound
blocks.body:
Let \(N,Q,k\) be nonnegative integers. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive perturbation.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
Write \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\) for the contraction parameter and
\(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\) for the signed-depth reward-amplitude constant. For an
alternative \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\) in the signed-depth family of
\cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} and any observed prefix
\(o=(a_1,y_1,\ldots,a_k,y_k)\), let \(\pi_{N,Q,v}(o)\) be the raw
terminal-depth posterior: the run-local unnormalized filter mass at latent
depth \(Q\), divided by the total run-local unnormalized filter mass of the
prefix. Then
\[
\pi_{N,Q,v}(o)
\le
\frac{\alpha^Q}
{\left\{1-c_0\left(\frac{\alpha}{1-c_0}\right)^Q\right\}^Q}.
\]

blocks.title: Rare-action second moment
blocks.body:
Let \(Q,k\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Time scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap exponent.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radius constant.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
Write \(L=\exp(\zeta)\), let \(\ell=\min\{Q,k\}\), and consider the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} at horizon \(k+1\). For an action/reward-symbol prefix
\[
o=((a_1,y_1),\ldots,(a_k,y_k)),
\]
let \(\pi_k^v(o)\) be its prefix mass under this model, and define the rare-action-history factor from \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities} by
\[
\mathfrak a_k(o)
=
L^{-(Q-\ell)}
\prod_{i:\,k-\ell<i\le k}\mathbf 1\{a_i=1\},
\]
with the empty product equal to one. Then
\[
\sum_{o}\pi_k^v(o)\,\mathfrak a_k(o)^2
=
L^{-2(Q-\ell)}
\left(\frac{1}{L}\right)^{|\{i:\ k-\ell<i\le k\}|},
\]
where the sum ranges over all action/reward-symbol prefixes of length \(k\).

blocks.title: Finite observed KL bound
blocks.body:
Let \(T,Q\in\mathbb N\) and \(t_0,\zeta,C,K_0\in\mathbb R\).  Write \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\), \(L=e^\zeta\), \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\), and \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(C>1\), and \(K_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform terminal posterior.)} For every horizon \(N\), every alternative index \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), every time \(t<N\), and every observed prefix \(o\) of actions and two-symbol rewards before \(t\), the finite conditional terminal-depth probability \(q_t^v(o)\) from \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities} satisfies
\[
q_t^v(o)\le K_0\alpha^Q .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the finite observed-word laws of the signed-depth alternatives of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}, taken before the reward symbols are decoded as real rewards, satisfy
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{fin},T}\middle\|\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{fin},T}\right)
\le
\frac{4c_0^2K_0^2}{1-c_0^2}\,
T\,\varepsilon_C^2\,\alpha^{2Q}\,L^{-Q}.
\]

blocks.title: Uniform bootstrap factor
blocks.body:
Let \(t_0>0\) and write \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\), \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\), \(\eta_0=\alpha/(1-c_0)\). Then there exists \(K_0>0\) such that
\[
\frac{1}{\bigl(1-c_0\bigl(\alpha/(1-c_0)\bigr)^{Q}\bigr)^{Q}}
\le
K_0
\qquad(Q\in\mathbb N).
\]

blocks.title: Terminal signed mass invariant
blocks.body:
Let \(N,Q,k\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and consider the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}.  For an observed prefix \(o=((a_i,y_i))_{i=1}^k\), write \(\lambda_v(h;o)\) for the unnormalized filter mass of terminal hidden state \(h\), write \(J(h)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\) and \(U(h)\in\{-1,+1\}\) for its depth and sign coordinates, and set
\[
\varepsilon_C=\min\left\{\frac{C-1}{2},\frac12\right\}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive initial scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap exponent.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Nontrivial overlap radius.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
With \(L=e^\zeta\), define the depth-\(Q\) action-history factor
\[
a^{(Q)}(o)
=
L^{-\max\{Q-k,0\}}
\prod_{\substack{1\le i\le k\\ i>k-\min\{Q,k\}}}
\mathbf 1\{a_i=1\}.
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{h:\,J(h)=Q} U(h)\lambda_v(h;o)
=
\varepsilon_C\,a^{(Q)}(o)
\sum_{h:\,J(h)=Q}\lambda_v(h;o).
\]

blocks.title: Next reward numerator
blocks.body:
Let \(U,k,N,Q\in\mathbb N\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and consider the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} with horizon \(N\), terminal depth \(Q\), initial weights \(p_v\), behavior policy \(b\), and reward-symbol/hidden-state kernel \(K_v\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive time scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive behavior perturbation.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap radius.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
Write
\[
c_0(t_0)=\frac{1-\alpha}{4},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is the signed-depth mixing parameter, and write \(\phi(0)=-1\), \(\phi(1)=1\).  For any observed action/reward-symbol prefix \(o\in(\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\})^k\), let
\[
\lambda_v(h;o)
\]
denote the unnormalized signed-depth filter mass, after the prefix \(o\), assigned to observed state \(0\) and packed hidden state \(h\in\{0,\ldots,2(Q+1)-1\}\).  Decode the packed hidden state by
\[
J(h)=\bigl\lfloor h/2\bigr\rfloor,
\qquad
U(h)=
\begin{cases}
+1, & h \equiv 1 \pmod 2,\\
-1, & h \equiv 0 \pmod 2.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{\tau}
\mathbf 1\!\left\{ ((a_i,r_i))_{i=1}^k(\tau)=o\right\}
\,\omega_v(\tau)\,\phi\!\left(r_{k+1}(\tau)\right)
=
v\,c_0(t_0)
\sum_{h=0}^{2(Q+1)-1}
\mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\,U(h)\,\lambda_v(h;o),
\]
where the outer sum is over all finite signed-depth trajectories \(\tau\) of horizon \(U+k+1\), and \(\omega_v(\tau)\) is their chronological path weight under \(p_v\), \(b\), and \(K_v\).

blocks.title: Terminal prefix mass identity
blocks.body:
Let \(U,k,Q\in\mathbb N\) with \(U\ge 1\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), let \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and consider the finite signed-depth model of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} at horizon \(U+k\).  For an action/reward-symbol prefix \(o\) of length \(k\), define the joint prefix-and-terminal-depth mass at the cut after the first \(k\) epochs by
\[
m_v^Q(o)
=
\Pr_v\{(A_1,R_1),\ldots,(A_k,R_k)=o,\ J_{k+1}=Q\}.
\]
For each hidden coordinate \(h\in\{0,\ldots,2(Q+1)-1\}\), let \(J(h)=\lfloor h/2\rfloor\), and let \(\lambda_v(h;o)\) be the unnormalized filter mass, as in \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities}, assigned after observing \(o\) to the cut state with hidden coordinate \(h\).  Then
\[
m_v^Q(o)
=
\sum_{h=0}^{2(Q+1)-1}
\mathbf 1\{J(h)=Q\}\,\lambda_v(h;o).
\]

blocks.title: Conditional reward mean identity
blocks.body:
Let \(T,Q\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(v\) be a Boolean alternative, written through
\[
\sigma(v)=
\begin{cases}
1, & v=\mathrm{true},\\
-1, & v=\mathrm{false}.
\end{cases}
\]
Assume
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive baseline.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive policy scale.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap radius.)} \(C>1\).
\end{itemize}
For every epoch \(t<T\) and every observed prefix \(o\in\{\,\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\,\}^{t}\times\{0,1\}^{t}\), the conditional next-reward mean satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_v[Y_t\mid \mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}=o]
=
\sigma(v)\,c_0(t_0)\,\varepsilon_C(C)\,
a_t^{(Q)}(o)\,q_t^v(o),
\]
where the left-hand side is the totalized ratio defining the finite-prefix conditional reward mean, \(c_0(t_0)=(1-\alpha)/4\), \(\varepsilon_C(C)=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\), and \(a_t^{(Q)}(o)\) and \(q_t^v(o)\) are the rare-action-history factor and terminal posterior of \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities}.

blocks.title: Observed signed-depth law
blocks.body:
For \(T,Q\in\mathbb N\), \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and two-point alternative index \(v\), define
\[
\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{obs},T}
\]
to be the observed-path law obtained by applying the observed-coordinate projection to the trajectory law of the embedded finite signed-depth model with horizon \(T\), parameters \((t_0,\zeta,C,Q)\), and alternative index \(v\).

blocks.title: Observed-path KL bound
blocks.body:
Fix \(t_0>0\), and write \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\). There exists a constant \(K_0>0\), depending on \(t_0\), such that whenever the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap exponent.)} \(\zeta>0\), and \(L=\exp(\zeta)\).
\item \textbf{(Reset amplitude.)} \(C>1\), and \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\).
\item \textbf{(Sequential ignorability.)} For every horizon \(T\), terminal depth \(Q\ge 1\), and alternative \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the signed-depth experiment in \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} satisfies \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability}.
\item \textbf{(Stationary start.)} For every horizon \(T\), terminal depth \(Q\ge 1\), and alternative \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the signed-depth experiment in \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} satisfies \cref{obj:ass:stationary-start}.
\end{itemize}
there exists a constant \(B_0>0\), depending on \(t_0,\zeta,C\), such that for every \(T\) and every \(Q\ge 1\), with \(\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\) denoting the observed-path law of the signed-depth alternative \(v\),
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\middle\|\,\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\right)
\le
B_0\,T\,\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}.
\]
Moreover, for each \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), each \(t<T\), and each observed prefix \(o\in\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the conditional reward mean satisfies the exact finite-prefix identity
\[
\mathbb E_v[Y_t\mid \mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}=o]
=
v\,c_0\,\varepsilon_C\,a_t^{(Q)}(o)\,q_t^v(o),
\]
where \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\), and \(a_t^{(Q)}\) and \(q_t^v\) are the rare-action-history factor and terminal-depth posterior from \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities}. The posterior satisfies
\[
q_t^v(o)\le K_0\,\alpha^Q .
\]
The same observed-path laws also satisfy
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\middle\|\,\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\right)
\le
\frac{4c_0^2K_0^2}{1-c_0^2}\,
T\,\varepsilon_C^2\,\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}.
\]

blocks.title: Stationary PHIW score mean
blocks.body:
Let \(T,n_X,n_H,k\in\mathbb N\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M\) be a raw POMDP experiment. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Mature time.)} \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\) and \(k\le t\).
\end{itemize}
Then the depth-\(k\) score \(Z_t(k)\) of \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}, evaluated under the observed trajectory law of \(M\), satisfies
\[
\int Z_t(k)\,d\mathbb P_M^{\mathrm{obs}}
=
\sum_s d_b(s)\,(P_e^k g_e)(s).
\]
Here \(d_b\) is the stationary law selected for the behavior-policy transition matrix
\[
P_b(s,s')=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} b(a\mid x_s)\,K(s,a)\{(r,s''):\ s''=s'\},
\]
and \(P_e^k g_e\) is the \(k\)-fold iterate of the target-policy transition operator applied to the target-policy reward regression
\[
g_e(s)=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} e(a\mid x_s)\int r\,K(s,a)(d r,d s').
\]

blocks.title: Target value is bounded
blocks.body:
Let \(T\ge 1\), let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let
\(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\in
\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) be a model in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Assume the model satisfies the stationary-start, sequential-ignorability, POMDP-kernel, bounded-reward, latent-stationary-overlap, and policy-overlap conditions of
\cref{obj:ass:stationary-start,obj:ass:sequential-ignorability,obj:ass:pomdp-kernel,obj:ass:bounded-reward,obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap,obj:ass:policy-overlap}. Then the stationary target-policy mean reward \(\theta(K,e)\) of \cref{obj:def:target-value} lies in the unit interval:
\[
\theta(K,e)\in[-1,1].
\]

blocks.title: Radius-sensitive PHIW risk
blocks.body:
For every trajectory length \(T\), observable alphabet size \(n_X\), latent alphabet size \(n_H\), and history depth \(k\), let
\[
\alpha=\exp\{-(1/t_0)\},\qquad L=\exp\{\zeta\},\qquad q_C=\frac{C-1}{C}.
\]
Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Mixing scale.)} \(0<t_0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap scale.)} \(0<\zeta\).
\item \textbf{(Radius parameter.)} \(1\le C\), with \(q_C\) as in \cref{obj:def:overlap-distance-radius}.
\item \textbf{(Trajectory length.)} \(1\le T\).
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} The experiment \(M\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(History depth.)} \(k\le T/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then the clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimator \(\widehat\theta_k\) from \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator}, evaluated under the observed trajectory law induced by \(M\), satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_M\!\left[\{\widehat\theta_k-\theta(K,e)\}^2\right]
\le
4q_C^2\alpha^{2k}
+\frac{2}{T}\left\{
L^{k+1}\left(1+\frac{4}{L-1}\right)
+\frac{4}{1-\alpha}
\right\},
\]
where \(\theta(K,e)\) is the stationary target-policy mean reward from \cref{obj:def:target-value}.

blocks.title: Observed KL radius bound
blocks.body:
Let \(t_0>0\).  Define
\[
\alpha(t_0)=\exp(-1/t_0),\qquad
c_0(t_0)=\frac{1-\alpha(t_0)}{4}.
\]
Then there exists a constant \(K_0=K_0(t_0)>0\) such that, for every \(\zeta>0\), \(C>1\), \(T\in\mathbb N\), and \(Q\in\mathbb N\) with \(Q\ge1\), if
\[
\varepsilon_C=\min\left\{\frac{C-1}{2},\frac12\right\},\qquad
L(\zeta)=\exp(\zeta),
\]
and if \(q_C\) is the radius in \cref{obj:def:overlap-distance-radius}, then
\[
\frac{q_C}{2}\le \varepsilon_C \le q_C
\]
and the observed-path laws \(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\) and
\(\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\) of the signed-depth alternatives satisfy
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\middle\|\,
\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}
\right)
\le
\frac{4c_0(t_0)^2K_0^2}{1-c_0(t_0)^2}\,
T\,\varepsilon_C^2\,\alpha(t_0)^{2Q}\,L(\zeta)^{-Q}.
\]

blocks.title: Parametric pair target value
blocks.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(v\in\{0,1\}\), and define the sign
\[
\sigma(v)=
\begin{cases}
+1, & v=1,\\
-1, & v=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Put
\[
\eta_T=\frac{1}{4\sqrt T},
\]
with value \(0\) when \(T=0\). Suppose the scalar parameters satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Initial scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap scale.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radius scale.)} \(C\ge 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(M_T^v\) be the singleton-state finite experiment with one observed state and one hidden state, fair behavior and target policies \(b(a\mid x_\star)=e(a\mid x_\star)=1/2\), reward support \(\{-1,+1\}\), and reward-transition kernel that assigns, from every state-action pair, probability
\[
\frac{1+\sigma(v)y\eta_T}{2}
\]
to reward \(y\in\{-1,+1\}\) and next state \((x_\star,h_\star)\). Then the stationary target-policy mean reward of \cref{obj:def:target-value}, evaluated in this experiment, satisfies
\[
\theta(K_{M_T^v},e_{M_T^v})=\sigma(v)\eta_T .
\]

blocks.title: Observed KL budget
blocks.body:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(T\ge 1\), and set \(\eta_T=1/(4\sqrt T)\). Let \(M_T^{-}\) and \(M_T^{+}\) be the two finite singleton-state experiments with one observed state \(x_\star\), one hidden state, initial mass at the single joint state, fair behavior and target policies \(b=e\) on \(\{0,1\}\), and reward code \(\mathsf r\in\{0,1\}\) decoded as \(2\mathsf r-1\). Under \(M_T^\sigma\), for \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), the reward-transition kernel returns to the single joint state and assigns reward \(y\in\{-1,+1\}\) probability
\[
\frac{1+\sigma y\eta_T}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P^{\mathrm{obs}}_{M_T^\sigma}\) for the image of the decoded trajectory law under the observed-path projection, the required KL budget holds in the direction
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
\mathbb P^{\mathrm{obs}}_{M_T^-}
\,\middle\|\,
\mathbb P^{\mathrm{obs}}_{M_T^+}
\right)
\le \frac14 .
\]

blocks.title: Observed risk bound
blocks.body:
Let \(T\ge 1\) and let \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\). Let \(\widehat\theta\) be an observable-data estimator of the admissible class used in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}: for each observed-alphabet size and policy pair, \(\widehat\theta\) is a measurable real-valued function of the observed path taking values in \([-1,1]\). For every
\[
M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\in \mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
\]
as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with \(\widehat\theta\) evaluated at the observed-alphabet size and policies of \(M\), the squared risk for the target value \(\theta(K,e)\) of \cref{obj:def:target-value} satisfies
\[
E_M\bigl[(\widehat\theta-\theta(K,e))^2\bigr]\le 4 .
\]

blocks.title: Two-point risk floor
blocks.body:
Let \(T\ge 1\), \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M_0,M_1\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  After identifying their common observed alphabet, write \(\mathbb P_j\) for the observed-data law of \(M_j\) and \(\theta_j\) for the target value of \(M_j\) from \cref{obj:def:target-value}, \(j\in\{0,1\}\).  Let \(s\) be a nonnegative separation radius and let \(\chi\) be a nonnegative KL upper bound.  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Common observable structure.)} The two models have the same observed-alphabet cardinality, the same behavior policy, and the same target policy.
\item \textbf{(Information bound.)} \(\mathbb P_0\ll\mathbb P_1\),
\[
\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_0\|\mathbb P_1)\le \chi,
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_0\|\mathbb P_1)<\infty .
\]
\item \textbf{(Target separation.)}
\[
2s\le |\theta_0-\theta_1| .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then every raw observable-data estimator \(\widehat\theta\), viewed as a real-valued measurable function of the observed-alphabet size, the policy pair, and the observed path, with \((\widehat\theta-\theta_j)^2\) integrable under \(\mathbb P_j\) at \(M_j\) for \(j=0,1\), satisfies
\[
\frac{s^2\exp(-\chi)}{4}
\le
\max\left\{
\mathbb E_{M_0}\!\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)^2\right],
\mathbb E_{M_1}\!\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_1)^2\right]
\right\}.
\]
Consequently, the minimax squared-error risk of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\frac{s^2\exp(-\chi)}{4}
\le
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C).
\]

blocks.title: Uniform parametric floor
blocks.body:
Fix a positive mixing scale \(t_0>0\) and a positive log-overlap scale \(\zeta>0\). For every horizon \(T\in\mathbb N\) with \(T\ge 1\) and every radius \(C\ge 1\), let \(M_T^{-}\) and \(M_T^{+}\) be the two raw POMDP experiments generated by the singleton-state, singleton-observation Rademacher construction with rewards in \(\{-1,+1\}\), fair behavior and target policies \(b=e\), and the two opposite signs of the construction's parametric reward tilt. Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class membership.)} Both \(M_T^{-}\) and \(M_T^{+}\) belong to the latent-overlap model class \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Common policies.)} Each experiment has equal behavior and target policies, and the two experiments share these policies:
\[
b_{M_T^{-}}=e_{M_T^{-}},
\qquad
b_{M_T^{+}}=e_{M_T^{+}},
\qquad
b_{M_T^{-}}=b_{M_T^{+}},
\qquad
e_{M_T^{-}}=e_{M_T^{+}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Uniform minimax floor.)} The minimax squared-error risk \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\frac{\exp(-1/4)}{64T}\le R_T(t_0,\zeta,C).
\]
\item \textbf{(Pointwise two-experiment floor.)} For every observable-data estimator \(\widehat\theta\), viewed as a measurable function of the revealed alphabet and the policies, under the usual squared-error integrability conditions for the observed trajectory laws of \(M_T^{-}\) and \(M_T^{+}\),
\[
\frac{\exp(-1/4)}{64T}
\le
\max\left\{
\mathbb E_{M_T^{-}}^{\mathrm{obs}}
\left[
\left(\widehat\theta(1,b_{M_T^{-}},e_{M_T^{-}};\mathsf O_T)-\theta(K_{M_T^{-}},e_{M_T^{-}})\right)^2
\right],
\mathbb E_{M_T^{+}}^{\mathrm{obs}}
\left[
\left(\widehat\theta(1,b_{M_T^{+}},e_{M_T^{+}};\mathsf O_T)-\theta(K_{M_T^{+}},e_{M_T^{+}})\right)^2
\right]
\right\},
\]
where \(\theta(K,e)\) is the stationary target-policy mean reward of \cref{obj:def:target-value}.
\end{itemize}
